MANILA, Philippines – Typhoon Rosal (Champi) is now less likely to bring significant rainfall to Batanes, the weather bureau said on Friday afternoon, October 23.

But scattered rain and thunderstorms can still hit Batanes, Cagayan, Isabela, Ilocos Norte, Ilocos Sur, La Union, the Cordillera Administrative Region, Palawan, Masbate, the Visayas, the Zamboanga Peninsula, Misamis Occidental, Camiguin, Surigao del Norte, Dinagat Islands, Basilan, and Tawi-Tawi in the next 24 hours, due to Rosal’s outer rainbands and the trough or extension of the typhoon.

Rosal was already 385 kilometers north northeast of Itbayat, Batanes, as of 4 pm on Friday. It is moving north northwest at 20 kilometers per hour (km/h), and is expected to leave the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR) on Saturday morning, October 24.
So far, the typhoon has maximum sustained winds of 155 km/h and gustiness of up to 190 km/h. At its peak, Rosal was a super typhoon with maximum sustained winds of 215 km/h.

The Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical, and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) has yet to lift tropical cyclone wind signals for portions of Northern Luzon. These areas are still under wind signals as of 5 pm on Friday:
Gale-force winds (62 to 88 km/h), minor to moderate threat to life and property

blocks.text: After Rosal’s exit from PAR, it may weaken into a severe tropical storm by Sunday morning, October 25.

Rosal, which entered PAR on Tuesday, October 20, is the Philippines’ 18th tropical cyclone for 2026, and the first for October. PAGASA earlier estimated the country may have one or two tropical cyclones during the month.
The Philippines is currently in a transition period to the northeast monsoon or amihan, following the end of the southwest monsoon or habagat, which was announced last October 5.

The northeast monsoon typically brings surges of cold temperatures, but the upcoming amihan period could be warmer as the existing strong El Niño in the tropical Pacific Ocean is predicted to become very strong in the fourth quarter of 2026. – Rappler.com
